title: Why this blog exists
description: I'm starting a public notebook to document what I'm learning and researching - from systems programming and computer science to philosophy. Here's what to expect.

content.description: I read and build constantly, but until now none of that thinking has had a permanent home. This blog is my public notebook - a place to document what I'm learning and researching, from computer science to anything i find interesting.

content.text: My interests don't stay in one lane. One week it's systems programming - Go schedulers, Rust ownership, real-time data pipelines. The next it's a philosophy text that reframes how I think about the systems I build. Writing is how I find out whether I actually understand something, so this blog will cover both ends and the connections between them.

list: Notes on CS topics I'm studying - systems, networking, cryptography, language design
Philosophy reading notes and the questions they leave me with
Research write-ups and experiments from my own projects
Occasional retrospectives on things I built and what they taught me

content.text: Explaining something forces a level of honesty that private notes never do. If I can't write it clearly, I don't understand it yet. Publishing also leaves a trail - a record of how my thinking changes over time, which feels especially fitting for someone who took everything apart as a kid just to see how it worked.

quote.text: I cannot teach anybody anything. I can only make them think.

content.text: Posts here are working notes, not polished essays. Expect them to be revised as I learn more - each post shows an updated date when that happens. If something here is wrong, I'd genuinely like to know: tell me.
